problem.title: The problem in four numbers
problem.lede: Feed decides whether a small poultry farm makes money. Smallholders in northern Nigeria pay too much for feed of uncertain quality.

feedShare.title: of poultry input costs is feed
feedShare.body: Feed is the biggest bill on the farm. Every naira saved on feed goes straight to the farmer.
feedShare.chartLabel: Ring chart: feed is 65 to 70 per cent of input costs.

diesel.title: Diesel price per litre
diesel.body: Bagged feed is milled far away and priced on diesel. When the pump price moves, the bag price follows.
diesel.chartLabel: Bar chart: average diesel price rose from 1,758 naira per litre in May 2025 to 3,277 naira in May 2026.

aflatoxin.title: in every 100 small-mill feed samples carried aflatoxin B1
aflatoxin.body: Samples came from in-house farm mills across 12 states. Groundnut cake was the main source.
aflatoxin.chartLabel: Grid of 100 squares, 83 of them highlighted: 83 per cent of samples carried aflatoxin B1.

scale.title: Own-mill break-even
scale.caption: Smallholders are over 60% of the sector
scale.body: Milling your own feed only pays at around 8,000 layers. Most smallholders are nowhere near that.
scale.chartLabel: Bar chart: own-mill break-even at 8,000 layers, compared with a 300-bird flock.

problem.statement: Quality-controlled milling only exists at a scale smallholders cannot reach — and the energy it runs on keeps getting more expensive.

how.title: Sunlight, software and a schedule
how.lede: A hub is a small feed mill shared by a cluster of 30–40 farmers. Three parts work together to make good feed cheaper.

parts.title: Sunlight drives the mill
parts.body: An 11 kWp solar array powers a 7.5 kW hammer mill and a 500 kg vertical mixer through solar motor drives. No diesel, and no large battery bank.

parts.title: Software guards quality
parts.body: Every maize and groundnut-cake lot is tested for moisture and aflatoxin at intake. Lots above 13% moisture or 20 µg/kg aflatoxin are blocked from any batch.

parts.title: Scheduling replaces storage
parts.body: Grinding is queued for the strongest-sun hours. Mixing and bagging fill the rest of the day. Least-cost formulas update with weekly local ingredient prices.

items.q: Is a SolarFeed hub running today?
items.a: Not yet. The hub hardware is specified and the research and host partners are identified; hub one is the pilot we are raising for. The images on this site are illustrations. The software builds on the offline-first stack Swifter already runs in production in other products.

items.q: How do you keep aflatoxin out of the feed?
items.a: Every maize and groundnut-cake lot gets a moisture reading and an aflatoxin rapid test at intake. The software will not let a lot into a batch above 13% moisture or 20 µg/kg aflatoxin, and monthly laboratory tests confirm the results.

items.q: Can I bring my own grain?
items.a: Yes. Farmers can bring their own grain for tested milling and mixing, or prepay for hub mash. Either way, every lot is tested before it is used.

items.q: What happens on cloudy days and during Harmattan?
items.a: Grinding is scheduled into the strongest-sun hours, panels are cleaned weekly in the dust season, and the hub keeps about three days of buffer stock.
Funders, farmer cooperatives, state livestock programmes, feed ingredient suppliers and equipment fabricators. Email us to talk about hubs two through ten.

hero.title: A small mill that runs on sunlight and checks its own grain
hero.lede: A SolarFeed hub is a micro feed mill shared by 30–40 farmers. Solar power, a software quality gate and a sun-aware schedule work together, so a smallholder gets feed made the way a large farm makes it.

parts.title: Sunlight drives the mill
parts.body: The hub’s heavy work — grinding and mixing — runs directly on solar power. Solar motor drives match the motors to what the panels are producing, so the hub needs no large battery bank and no diesel generator.

hero.lede: Why a shared solar feed hub matters for farmers, for food safety and for northern Nigeria’s grain economy. Every figure on this page has a source listed at the bottom.

environment.title: Taking diesel out of milling
environment.body: Bagged feed is milled far away and priced on diesel. A hub mills on sunlight, close to the farms it serves, from grain grown nearby.

points.title: No diesel in the mill
points.body: The hammer mill and mixer run on an 11 kWp solar array through solar motor drives.

points.title: Shorter journeys
points.body: Grain goes from local farms to a local hub and back as feed, instead of to a distant mill.

points.title: Measured, not assumed
points.body: The pilot targets energy cost and CO₂ per tonne at least 50% below diesel, including transport, and will publish the result either way.

environment.evidence: The evidence so far is mixed. Solar milling pilots in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania found a remaining viability gap against diesel (Efficiency for Access, CLASP and Energy 4 Impact, 2020). A 2025 analysis found PV-powered milling can be more cost-effective than diesel in sub-Saharan Africa (Falama and Sun, 2025). Hub one is designed to find out which holds in Katsina.

safety.body: In a 12-state study, 83% of feed from in-house farm mills carried aflatoxin B1. A hub tests every maize and groundnut-cake lot at intake and blocks any lot above 13% moisture or 20 µg/kg aflatoxin.

privacy.title: Your data, in plain language
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal data SolarFeed Hubs collects through this website, why, how long we keep it and how to see or delete it. SolarFeed Hubs is a project of Swifter Ventures LTD (CAC RC 8894875), which is the data controller. We follow the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.

sections.title: What we collect
paragraphs: When you send the enquiry form: your full name, organisation, role, email address, phone number (if you give it), what kind of partner you are, your message and your consent.
We do not use analytics, advertising trackers or cookies. Your browser remembers your language choice on your own device only.
Like every website, our hosting provider records technical logs such as IP addresses to keep the site running and secure. Our fonts are served from our own site, so no third party sees your visit.

sections.title: Why we collect it
paragraphs: To read and reply to your enquiry, and to follow up on a partnership you asked about. Our lawful basis is your consent, which you give with the tick box on the form.
We never sell your data and never use it for advertising.

sections.title: Where it is stored
paragraphs: Enquiries are stored in a database run by our provider, Supabase. Its servers may be outside Nigeria. Where data leaves Nigeria, we rely on the safeguards the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 requires for cross-border transfers. Only the SolarFeed Hubs team can read enquiries.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: We keep an enquiry for up to 24 months after our last contact with you, then delete it. If you ask us to delete it sooner, we will.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask to see the data we hold about you, correct it, delete it, or withdraw your consent at any time. Withdrawing consent does not affect anything we did before you withdrew it.
If you are not happy with how we handle your data, you can complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC).

sections.title: Farmer data at the hub
paragraphs: Data collected at a hub — orders, ingredient tests and batch records — is handled with each farmer’s consent under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and anonymised before any research data is published. Farmers will receive a separate plain-language notice, in English and Hausa, when the hub opens.

sections.title: Contact us
paragraphs: To see, correct or delete your data, email isfagachi@gmail.com or write to Swifter Ventures LTD, No. 3 Ibrahim Coomassie Road, New GRA, Ring Road, Katsina, Katsina State, Nigeria.
